title: "We Have to Hit Our Numbers": The Order Behind the WorldCom Fraud

lines.say: Third quarter, two thousand. WorldCom can't meet Wall Street's expectations, and its line costs come in almost one billion dollars higher than expected.
lines.show: Third quarter, 2000. WorldCom can't meet Wall Street's expectations, and its line costs come in almost $1 billion higher than expected.

lines.say: The finance chief, Scott Sullivan, tells CEO Bernard Ebbers they should warn investors. According to the appeals court, Ebbers refuses.
His answer, as the appeals court described the trial evidence: we have to hit our numbers.

scene.cite: As quoted in U.S. v. Ebbers, 2d Cir., 2006

lines.say: Ebbers had borrowed over four hundred million dollars against his WorldCom stock.
lines.show: Ebbers had borrowed over $400 million against his WorldCom stock.

lines.say: Over the next year and a half, about three point eight billion dollars in expenses were booked as capital.
lines.show: Over the next year and a half, about $3.8 billion in expenses were booked as capital.

lines.say: In two thousand five, a jury convicted him on all nine counts. Twenty-five years.
lines.show: In 2005, a jury convicted him on all nine counts. 25 years.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
